_what: How a tool's own samples (verify rows of kind sample-run) are run where its placement runs it, by the placement's executor (src/workshop-sample-rules.mjs, used by src/workshop.mjs sampleChecked, describe and publish). A placement whose executor has no row runs its samples as before. `safe`: the only kinds of sample allowed there, each sample saying its own `safety`; a sample that names another is refused before it runs, at save and at every run. A `dry-run` sample sets the tool's own boolean input `dry_run_field` to true, so it shows what it would do and does nothing. `unconnected: owed`: when the computer the placement names is not connected, the sample is not failed; it is recorded as owed until `owed_until`, with the tests the sample names as its `evidence`, and it runs by itself the first time that computer connects (its agent publishes its card). `readback`: how an account that did not publish the tool proves a published one: describe-only, because a run needs that account's own computer. Words are what a person or an AI reads.

words.unsafe: {tool} runs on the person's own computer, so each of its sample-run checks must say its safety: {safe}. Give the sample "safety": "read-only" when it only reads, or "dry-run" with {field}: true when it would act.
words.dry_run: {tool}'s dry-run sample must set its boolean input {field} to true, so the sample shows what it would do and does nothing.
words.owed: Owed: it runs on the first computer this account connects.
